entries.03f5ad397fefb88e: This division handles Western confectionery, such as cakes and desserts. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥163,209 million (103.8% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). The key two-piece fresh cake was firm, and products such as “Ichigo Special,” “Double Roll” and “Funwari Waffle” grew, and products for convenience stores also performed well. Fujiya Co., Ltd. operates a chain of Western confectionery specialty stores and manufactures and sells cakes and desserts.

entries.1daaa157673aad6c: This division handles Japanese confectionery, and has the smallest revenue of the six divisions. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥81,333 million (106.1% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). Kushi-dango, daifuku and manju performed well, and hotcakes with improved quality, Yamazaki Mushi Pan and chūka-man also grew, while the Yukidora series of chilled products contributed to sales.
entries.2bad200c1958edad: This business provides logistics, design, supervision and construction contracting for food manufacturing facilities, clerical contracting and outsourcing services, non-life insurance agency business, and the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for food manufacturing machinery and equipment, among other activities. Yamazaki Logistics Co., Ltd. and Sun Logistics Co., Ltd. handle transport between plants and sales offices and deliveries to customers; Yamazaki Engineering Co., Ltd. handles the design, supervision and construction of food manufacturing equipment; Yamazaki Co., Ltd. handles non-life insurance agency business; and Yamazaki Clean Service Co., Ltd. manufactures and sells cleaning agents. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥15,699 million (106.2% of the previous consolidated fiscal year), and in addition, intersegment internal revenue or transfers amounted to ¥51,224 million.
entries.3644852dc10d9165: This business provides logistics, design, supervision and construction contracting for food manufacturing facilities, clerical contracting and outsourcing services, non-life insurance agency business, and the manufacture and sale of cleaning agents for food manufacturing machinery and equipment, among other activities.
entries.3c4a8bee5db55372: This division handles biscuits, snacks, rice crackers, confectionery and other products. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥195,256 million (106.9% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). Fujiya Co., Ltd.'s “Country Ma'am” and “Home Pie” grew strongly, and snack products such as Yamazaki Biscuits Co., Ltd.'s “Chipstar” and Tohato Co., Ltd.'s “Caramel Corn” also grew. Rice crackers (arare, senbei, etc.) are manufactured by Suehiro Seika Co., Ltd. and Akita Inafuku Beika Co., Ltd., and are mainly sold by YAMAZAKI BAKING CO., LTD.
entries.54fd031e898c138f: This is the largest of the six divisions in the food business by revenue. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥484,674 million (104.3% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). Key products such as “Marugoto Sausage,” Lunch Pack and “Apple Pie” grew, and low-priced products such as the “Zusshiri” series and “Donut Station” also grew. Sales of YK Baking Company Co., Ltd., which utilizes Yamazaki's technology, were also strong, significantly exceeding the previous fiscal year's sales.
entries.5906b9d3cca8be0f: This business manufactures bread, Japanese and Western confectionery, prepared breads and cooked rice products, and confectionery and rice crackers, and sells them to its own store formats, mass merchandisers, convenience stores and other retail outlets. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,215,940 million (105.4% of the previous consolidated fiscal year), accounting for the majority of consolidated revenue of ¥1,311,430 million. The bakery business, which makes frozen dough for bread and other products, in-store manufacturing and retail at group companies' directly operated stores, the multi-store expansion of bakery cafés, and bread businesses in the United States and Southeast Asia are also included in this business. The group as a whole consists of YAMAZAKI BAKING CO., LTD., 57 subsidiaries and 4 affiliates. Sales are disclosed in six categories: plain bread, sweet bread, Japanese confectionery, Western confectionery, prepared breads and cooked rice products, and confectionery, rice crackers and other products.

entries.6c2bc0ad7cdf1e43: This division handles loaf bread. Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥118,287 million (103.7% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). In January 2025, Royal Bread, the key product whose quality was improved with a new technology, grew, and low-priced products, including chain-specific products made with this technology, and bread for sandwiches also performed well. Double Soft was also relaunched in November with its quality improved by new technology.

entries.b5cdf2a0abc0f0a2: This business operates convenience stores and food supermarkets. The Daily Yamazaki Business Headquarters of YAMAZAKI BAKING CO., LTD. operates convenience stores on a franchise basis, and Super Yamazaki Co., Ltd. operates food supermarkets. These stores purchase and sell products of the YAMAZAKI BAKING Group. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥79,790 million (104.7% of the previous consolidated fiscal year). As of the end of December 2025, the total number of stores was 1,251: 998 “Daily Yamazaki,” 244 “New Yamazaki Daily Store” and 9 “Yamazaki Daily Store,” a decrease of 39 from the end of the previous year.
